jobs.description:
Are you a results-oriented commercial leader who thrives at the heart of the business?
As Managing Director of Damstahl, you will lead a market-leading sales organisation and hold overall responsibility for sales, market development and financial performance. The head office is located in Malmö, with sales offices in Gothenburg and Stockholm. Sweden is the largest market and has an established sales organisation led by a Sales Director. The Swedish business generates revenue of approximately SEK 800-900 million and has 30 employees, 16 of whom are focused on sales. Damstahl also has a sales office and warehouses in Sweden, Norway and one salesperson in Finland.
Your responsibilities will include:
• Identifying new market segments and business opportunities
• Strengthening Damstahl’s market position and developing the product mix in prioritised areas
• Representing Damstahl in business negotiations, industry forums and trade fairs
• Overall responsibility for the company’s operations and performance in 3 Nordic countries
• Ensure that the strategy is translated into specific objectives and action plans.
• Be the culture ambassador and ensure that the organization's structure and capabilities support current and future business needs
You will lead the Swedish, Norwegian and Finnish operations with a clear mandate strategically. You will refer to the Damstahl’s Group CEO. The role involves approximately two days of travel per week, enabling you to remain close to the organisation, the business and market developments.
What we offer
This role is ideal for a leader who wants to develop an organization with a strong sales focus and who is motivated by doing business and creating growth, while benefiting from the long-term perspective and stability of a successful and well-established company.
Damstahl’s ambition is to become one of Europe’s three leading distributors within its field. Its strategy is based on increasing market share, developing the product mix and identifying new areas of growth. Digitalization is an important part of Damstahl’s strategy and customer offering. Damstahl has a fully developed webshop, EDI and ERP integrations, and also offers AI-based services.
Who are you?
You are a results-oriented commercial leader who wants to stay close to the business. You understand how warehousing and logistics contribute to commercial success and can demonstrate, through documented results, that you have created profitable growth as a Sales Director or Managing Director within B2B—preferably in an industrial business with warehousing operations.
You have a strong ability to turn plans into action and can analyze market developments and the competitive landscape, translating these insights into clear commercial priorities. Experience from steel, metals, technical distribution or a related industrial sector is a significant advantage. Knowledge of tubes, fittings and flanges is particularly valuable, as this is a key area for growth. Fluency in spoken and written English and Swedish is required.
About Damstahl
Damstahl AB’s head office is located in Malmö, with sales offices in Gothenburg and Stockholm. The company also has a sales office in Norway and sales representation in Finland. Whilst the Damstahl Group has its headquarter in Skanderborg, Denmark.
Damstahl is part of the NEUMO Ehrenberg Group, a family-owned industrial group with approximately 2,250 employees and annual revenue of around EUR 800 million.
· Damstahl Group generates revenue of approximately EUR 350 million
· The Group has around 290 employees
· More than 70,000 tonnes of stainless steel are distributed annually
· Warehousing and distribution capacity is located in Denmark, Sweden and Norway
Damstahl’s competitive strength is built on extensive product expertise, high availability and a comprehensive Nordic and European warehousing and distribution network. We offer a broad and extensive range of stainless steel products, including sheets, bars, tubes, fittings and flanges. Through the Group, the offering also includes aluminium and other metals.
The Skanderborg facility includes an automated high-bay warehouse with capacity for approximately 10,000 tonnes of stainless steel The extensive warehousing structure ensures high product availability and short lead times across the Nordic markets. 
The Malmö facility includes a fully automated warehouse with the capacity of 4 400 m/2. The operation running from 7:00 AM to 4:00 PM with a total staff of five, plus three people handling logistics and returns, along with a Team Leader for that group. https://www.damstahl.com/sv/
Application
Damstahl is collaborating with Charlotte Olsson at Insikta AB on this recruitment. If you have any questions, please contact Charlotte Olsson on +46 70 602 19 11 or at charlotte@insikta.se.
Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis. Naturally, all enquiries and applications will be treated confidentially. To apply, simply submit your CV together with a brief explanation of why you are interested in the role.

Why Doktor.se
Doktor.se is Sweden's largest digital healthcare provider. We combine physical clinics with a digital platform serving millions of consultations per year across Sweden, Germany, and Norway. Our 25-person engineering team has startup autonomy inside a profitable, international organization with 1,000+ employees and over 1B SEK in revenue.
We run OpenAI and Anthropic models in production across patient and clinician workflows, and that footprint is growing fast.
What you'll do
Our infrastructure works, but it was built to solve yesterday's problems. We need someone who can help us get to where we want to be — not maintain what we have, but reshape it. If you want a place where everything is already figured out, this isn't it. If you want to build something better, here's what you'd own:

Build a deployment platform where teams ship their own services without asking you for permission.

Design infrastructure that is secure by default, so teams don't have to think about encryption, network isolation, or data residency. It just works.

Create deployment pipelines where security scanning, policy checks, and compliance happen automatically, invisible when everything is fine, loud when something needs attention.

Support and scale infrastructure for AI workloads, we run models in production across our platform, and that footprint is growing.

Set up observability that gives teams real insight into their own services, useful dashboards, alerts that mean something, not noise that everyone ignores.

Work closely with developers to understand what slows them down, and then fix it. Not by doing it for them, but by making it easy for them to do it themselves.

Maintain and evolve our cloud account structure, networking, and identity management across multiple regions and products.

You will report to to, and work close with, our Head of Product and Technology. You will be the go to person in technical strategical questions and the technical sounding board — advising on complex technical decisions and translating product/business direction into what's actually feasible.

Some weeks you'll write infrastructure code. Some weeks you'll pair with a developer to debug a slow service. Some weeks you'll design how a new product gets its own isolated infrastructure. The common thread: you make the teams around you better.
Make developers faster, not more dependent on you.
What we're looking for
You've built and operated Kubernetes in production. Not just deployed a Helm chart once, you've debugged networking issues, designed RBAC policies, and thought about how multiple teams share a cluster without stepping on each other.

You know AWS well. Accounts, networking, IAM, KMS. You have opinions about what should live in Kubernetes and what genuinely needs to be an AWS managed service, and you lean toward keeping things in Kubernetes where possible.

You've worked with GitOps and infrastructure as code. Flux, ArgoCD, Terrafor, specific tools matter less than the principle: infrastructure changes go through pull requests, are reviewed, and are auditable.

You understand developers because you are one. You can read their code, understand their pipelines, and have meaningful conversations about architecture.

You think about security as something you design into systems, not something you review at the end.

You have opinions, and you can change them when someone makes a better argument.

University degree in computer science, engineering, or equivalent experience.

Tech stack
Cloud - AWS (multi-account, multi-region)
Orchestration - Kubernetes / EKS
IaC - Terraform
CI/CD - GitHub Actions
Languages - Python, TypeScript
AI - OpenAI, Anthropic (in production and tooling)
Observability - Datadog / Grafana (you'll shape this)
What we offer
Real influence. You'll shape how our platform works, not just operate what someone else designed.

Healthcare context. Patient data, regulatory compliance, and real consequences for getting it wrong. What you build actually matters.

Small team, direct impact. 25 engineers, your work is visible, not lost in a machine.

Autonomy. No micromanagement, no endless approval chains.

AI in production. We're running LLMs in patient and clinician workflows today, the infrastructure needs to grow with that.

Collective agreement, 30 days vacation, wellness allowance, personal development budget.

Practical details
Start: As soon as we find the right person. We'll accommodate your notice period.

Employment: Permanent, full-time. Six month probation period.

Location: On-site, Monday–Thursday at Sveavägen 63, Stockholm. Fridays are flexible.

Language: English is our working language in tech. Swedish is a bonus.

Work permit: You must already have the right to work in Sweden.

Contact: Karin Bergström, Head of Product and technology

We handle recruitment internally — no agencies, no consultants, no external recruiters.

Job Scope 
High level purpose of function. 

A Vision Automation Engineer in a cell manufacturing company plays a key role in developing, optimizing, reverse-engineering, and maintaining machine vision and optical inspection systems to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient operations. They are responsible for programming, troubleshooting, and improving cameras, lighting configurations, and image processing algorithms, supporting both legacy production line re-commissioning and new vision system installations. The role also includes ensuring accurate data transfer, system connectivity, and smooth communication with PLCs, SCADA, and upper-level MES platforms to enable inline defect traceability, dimensional inspection, and digital integration. Close collaboration with production, engineering, and maintenance teams is required to identify and implement solutions that improve quality, throughput, and equipment uptime. A strong focus is placed on continuous improvement, safety, and scalability to meet the growing demand for electric vehicle battery production. 

Key Responsibilities 
Overall areas of responsibilities and activities 
Key responsibilities include (but are not limited to) 
Participate in HAZOP sessions and ensure compliance with process safety, operational safety, and environmental standards relating to equipment control and programming.  
Responsible for the FATs of the equipment (Project timeline dependent).  
Lead vision system integration and optical calibration during equipment commissioning and line re-starts (Project timeline dependent). 
Develop and reverse-engineer the vision inspection systems to be implemented in the production and logistics equipment in the factory, as well as the relevant specifications and documentation. 
Author and review engineering design documentation (Specifications, Functional design, Logic diagrams, Test Cases, Test Records).  
Train and mentor new engineers, and educate other support functions on machine vision, optics, and quality inspection gates. 
Code review and test of suppliers' vision software and algorithmic work within the projects to validate specified defect detection thresholds (Gauge R&R) and to ensure the quality and reliability of the data transferred from the equipment to the upper-level systems. 
Participate in R&D activities for piloting of new technologies and their suitability to production environments. 
Define and improve the factory blueprint, general specifications and ways of working in collaboration with the extended automation and digitalization teams. (Project timeline dependent). 
Contribute to technical improvements, development and optimization of software processes internally in the automation team 
The role requires regular presence on the production floor, with a minimum of approximately 25% of working hours spent on-site. Depending on project needs (such as line re-commissioning), there may be periods where up to 100% of working hours are required on the shop floor. 
Develop and maintain machine vision and image processing programming standards. 
Guide and mentor colleagues to industrial best practices, focussing on growth and development. 
Complete supplementary tasks as seen fit by management to effectively utilize time and resource for the benefit of the business. 

Requirements 
Educational background and previous experience required for the role 

Qualifications and Experience 
Bachelors Degree in Electronics, Mechatronics, Electrical, Automation, Robotics, Software Engineering or similar. 
Minimum of 3 years of relevant work experience within Industrial Automation in process-driven or discrete manufacturing industries such as: Battery Cell, Automotive, Chemical, Paper, Semiconductors, Pharma, Food, Warehouses, etc. 
Experience of working with industrial camera systems, optical components, and lighting techniques, including the selection, configuration, and calibration of camera hardware for manufacturing inspection and process control applications 
Experience in the design, configuration, and deployment of machine vision systems including cameras, lighting, and vision software platforms such as Cognex, Halcon, or equivalent, with experience integrating vision outputs into PLC, SCADA, and MES environments via OPC connectivity. 
Experience developing and optimising image processing pipelines and vision algorithms for applications such as defect detection, pattern recognition, and dimensional verification, with familiarity with industrial communication protocols for vision system integration. 
Experience in writing technical documentation including inspection requirement specifications, algorithm validation reports, vision system configuration records, functional design, UML, test cases, and test records. 
Experience with image processing software and programming tools relevant to industrial vision applications, such as Python, C++, OpenCV, or equivalent vision libraries, with the ability to develop, test, and optimise vision algorithms for real-time manufacturing environments 
Experienced continuous improvement and root cause analysis. 

Specific skills 
Strong knowledge of mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic systems. 
Knowledge of cybersecurity best practices for manufacturing systems. 
Troubleshooting skills with diagnostic equipment. 
Ability to document technical problems concisely. 
Excellent English skills, both written and oral, are essential. Basic Swedish and other language skills are a plus. You should have good communication skills and be able to work in close collaboration with colleagues from many different teams. 
Ability to work within varying environments including clean-rooms and dry-rooms, while wearing appropriate PPE. 
Comfortable operating in high-profile, international, and high-pressure environments. 
A genuine technical interest and passion about working within production is highly valued.

Company description:
Epiroc is a leading productivity partner for the mining, infrastructure and natural resources industries. Withcutting-edge technology, Epiroc develops and produces innovative drill rigs, rock excavation and constructionequipment, and provides world-class service and consumables. The company was founded in Stockholm,Sweden, and has passionate people supporting and collaborating with customers in more than 150 countries.Learn more at www.epirocgroup.com.
Job description:We’re looking for a Product Owner – AI & Test Engineering to join our SW Platform organization. We’re responsible for the machine platform that Epiroc’s mining and construction equipment runs on.
 In this role, AI is at the heart of what you do. You’ll help shape how software developers across all of Epiroc use AI in their daily work, and how AI changes the way we test and verify our software.
 Are you curious about how AI is changing software development? Do you enjoy collaborating with people across teams and helping turn needs into clear priorities? Would you like to help build something new from the start, with an impact across the whole company? Then we’d love to hear from you.
 A stream in the making
 AI & Test Engineering is a new product stream in our platform organisation. The teams are being built right now, and their setup, size and exact scope aren’t finalised yet. As Product Owner, you’ll have a real opportunity to influence how the stream takes shape, together with the teams, your manager and the Chief Product Owner.
 Your mission
 As Product Owner you’re responsible for the AI & Test Engineering product stream, where AI is the main focus. The stream is planned to cover two areas:
  AI Software Factory: exploring and introducing AI-supported, agentic ways of working across the software development lifecycle, for all software developers at Epiroc.
 AI-driven Test & Integration: using AI to rethink how we test and integrate platform software, together with test frameworks, simulation, a software-defined lab and system testing.
  
You connect the teams with their stakeholders. For the AI Software Factory, these are software developers and development teams across Epiroc’s divisions and sites. For Test & Integration, they are mainly the internal teams that develop and deliver on the platform.
 You’re responsible for the product backlog in Jira and the roadmap. By listening to stakeholders and understanding their needs, you help translate them into clear epics and user stories and support the teams in focusing on what creates the most value.
 You keep up with how AI in software development is evolving and help turn new possibilities into practical value for developers and testers.
 You work closely with the Scrum Masters and Tech Leads, collaborate with our architects and work closely with the Chief Product Owner on the overall platform roadmap. You also take part in cross-team planning together with the other product streams. You’ll report to a team manager in the SW Platform organization and be part of a supportive team where knowledge sharing and learning are encouraged.
Profile description:Your profile
  You have experience as a Product Owner or in a similar role, for example product manager, test lead, technical project lead or requirements owner, in a software development environment.
 You have a genuine interest in AI and how it can support software development and testing, and you may already use AI tools in your own work.
 You’re familiar with agile ways of working such as Scrum and with tools like Jira.
 You enjoy working with a broad range of stakeholders and helping new ways of working spread across an organization.
 It’s a plus if you have experience with AI-assisted or agentic software development, AI in testing, test automation, CI/CD or simulation.
 You speak Swedish and you’re fluent in English, both written and spoken.
  
As a person, you’re curious, structured, communicative and collaborative. You’re comfortable when not everything is decided yet, and you enjoy helping to create structure together with others. You build trusting relationships with stakeholders, help the teams find focus and like to keep learning.
 We know that great candidates don’t always meet every requirement. If this role sounds interesting, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t tick every box. We welcome applicants of all genders and backgrounds and believe diverse teams build better products.
 Location
 The role is based in Örebro, Sweden. We work hybrid, with at least three days a week in the office.
 Application and contacts
 Please send your application, including CV and personal letter, by creating an account in our recruitment system as soon as possible but no later than 27th of November.
 Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and the position may be filled before last application date. Please note that, due to the current regulations, we will only consider applications received through our system and not via email or social media.

jobs.description:
The Education Office (EdO) is one of SSE’s Professional Services units and consists of around 58 colleagues. As a central part of the SSE journey, we support and develop key academic services for students and stakeholders across our BSc, MSc, and PhD programs. Our work spans assessment, program management, scholarships, international collaborations, academic support, central course and exam coordination, as well as degrees and certificates.
We offer you
A diverse role at one of the top business schools in Europe with ambitious students and staff in a dynamic, academic environment. This role is ideal for a highly organized, people-oriented person who enjoys complex processes.
The role
We are looking for Admissions coordinator for our BSc programs. The successful candidate will belong to a team of Admissions & Program management at Education Office, reporting to Group Manager of that team.
Your tasks include, but are not limited to:
Coordinating application and admissions process for the BSc programs, ensuring an efficient, accurate and applicant-focused process.
Assessing applications, including eligibility, qualifications and supporting documentation, and participating actively in the selection of candidates.
Guiding prospective students and applicants regarding SSE, the BSc programs, admissions requirements and the application process.
Collaborating with faculty, and other internal and external stakeholders involved in admissions.
Contributing to recruitment and conversion activities for prospective and admitted students, including information sessions, events and other applicant-facing activities.
Supporting the Program Manager for the BSc in Business & Economics with diverse program-related tasks and activities, in accordance with the agreed division of responsibilities and based on the needs of the program.
Contributing to the continuous development of admissions processes, systems and ways of working, including the use of digital tools and AI where relevant.
Working in a dynamic organization where priorities, processes and responsibilities may evolve. You should therefore be comfortable adapting to change, taking on new tasks and contributing to developing new ways of working.
Occasional travel and participation in events outside regular office activities may occur.

Your profile
As Admissions Coordinator, you will be coordinating admissions process and processing applications and enquiries, often within fixed deadlines. You therefore need to be structured, detail-oriented and comfortable taking responsibility for processes from start to finish. You are proactive, flexible and able to prioritize while maintaining a high level of accuracy and service.
At the same time, admissions process is highly collaborative, and you enjoy working closely with colleagues, faculty and other stakeholders. The position involves contact with prospective students and applicants. You therefore have strong interpersonal and communication skills and can explain sometimes complex admissions requirements in a clear, professional and service-minded way. You are also comfortable handling challenging cases and communicating decisions consistently and respectfully. You are comfortable interpreting admissions requirements, assessing applicants and documentation against established criteria, and applying rules and procedures consistently.
Qualifications:
An academic education
Experience of, or a strong understanding of, admissions processes within Swedish higher education.
Experience of working with Swedish and international high school qualifications
Swedish and English, both spoken and written.

About the Center for wellbeing, welfare and happiness and research area
Wellbeing research examines how people experience and evaluate their lives, what enables them to thrive, and how individuals, organizations and societies can contribute to better lives. The field brings together perspectives from psychology, economics and behavioural science to understand different dimensions of wellbeing, including happiness, meaning in life and psychological richness. At the Center for Wellbeing, Welfare and Happiness (CWWH), we connect these questions to the development of knowledge that can inform policy and practice.
A central methodological challenge is how to capture the richness of people’s experiences through reliable and valid measures. Advances in natural language processing and large language models offer opportunities to complement traditional rating scales with systematic analyses of people’s own descriptions of their lives, emotions and experiences. This research combines wellbeing science, psychometrics and computational methods to investigate what language-based assessments can reveal about wellbeing, how they relate to established measures, and how they can capture differences between people and changes over time. The position will contribute to developing and validating these approaches, with relevance to the center’s research in Sweden and across countries.
The role
The postdoc will develop an independent research line on the measurement of wellbeing beyond traditional rating scales, with a focus on natural language (open-ended responses, text and speech) analyzed with computational methods, including large language models.
The postdoc will contribute to the center's work on wellbeing in Sweden and across nations, co-author with center researchers, and connect CWWH to international collaborators and funding opportunities. The role also includes active participation in the center's outreach, such as media, public lectures and events.

This period may be extended only where special circumstances apply. Professional proficiency in English (written and spoken) is a requirement. We expect the candidate to relocate to Stockholm.

A strong publication record in wellbeing science, including first-authored articles in leading international peer-reviewed journals

Demonstrated research independence and an established international research network
Documented experience communicating research to non-academic audiences, e.g., media, public lectures or popular science

Meritorious
Experience with assessment methods beyond self-report, e.g., implicit measures or automated coding of text
Development of open research software or openly shared models
Applied collaborations with organizations or industry, e.g., in work-related wellbeing or psychometrics

A curriculum vitae

Are you a Python programmer? Are you driven by system-level challenges? Join the Software Test Solutions at Westermo as a Software Developer!
Are you our next Software Developer?
Software Test Solutions develops our in-house test framework, which is used to test our products, and plays a critical role in ensuring product quality and reliability. Many teams rely on the accuracy of our test results, which makes our work essential for validating our products against their specifications.
We are looking for a software developer who thrives in an agile environment and wants to be part of a team that builds and maintains this framework and its tools. The framework is used for system-level testing of our products in network solutions, running on dedicated test systems.
Our department is made up of two teams: the Test Framework team (the role described here), which schedules and runs tests, processes the test results and maintains the test systems, and the Test Developer team, which develops and maintains tests for our operating system WeOS. We promote close collaboration between the two teams, so your work won't necessarily stay limited to the framework – there's plenty of room to explore and contribute across both.
In your role, you will be:

Programming primarily in Python (and Go), working with tools such as Docker and Kubernetes.

Analysing test results and troubleshooting and refining the framework to keep it reliable.

Maintaining and developing the test systems, with the devices under test, that the framework relies on.

Extending the framework to support new WeOS functionality.

Developing the next generation of our test framework to meet future demands on scalability, including virtual testing, and reduced complexity for end users.

Working with both front-end and back-end development of the web interfaces for configuration and visualization of test results.

We think about automation in everything we do, and we are always trying out new technologies that help us meet current and future demands. We use Jira for planning and tracking work, and keep improving our Agile methods. AI is also a natural part of our daily software work, and we are exploring how to put it to even better use.

You have an academic background in computer science or similar, and you’re motivated by solving real problems with smart solutions. We value teamwork, and hope you do, too. You enjoy both technical development and team collaboration, and you share your knowledge just as readily as you ask for help. You are curious and innovative, comfortable in an agile environment, and like to try, test, and learn with colleagues.
Further, we want you to be:

Experienced in Python development and eager to deepen your skills.

Comfortable working in a Linux environment.

Familiar with software engineering tools such as source code management, CI/CD, containers, and web development (front-end and/or back-end).

Interested in networking technologies.

Fluent in English and Swedish.

Oh, and don't worry, if you're not an expert in all the things described – you'll learn.
In return, we offer: You will be working at the forefront of technology in a friendly, open culture where you get the opportunity to learn from skilled colleagues every day. A mature and caring leadership in a flat organization. Through our collective bargain agreement you will be covered in terms of insurance, pension and other benefits. We like to have fun together and we regularly enjoy sports and other social activities as a team. We believe that magic happens when people meet. We are a learning organization and we truly love to try new things, think outside the box and be innovative together!

Architecture and requirements
Cyber security
Acceptance & verification
Commissioning

jobs.occupation: Academic Advisor to the Stockholm School of Economics
jobs.description:
The Education Office (EdO) is one of SSE’s Professional Services units and consists of around 58 colleagues. As a central part of the SSE journey, we support and develop key academic services for students and stakeholders across our BSc, MSc, and PhD programs. Our work spans assessment, program management, scholarships, international collaborations, academic support, central course and exam coordination, as well as degrees and certificates.
We are looking for an Academic Advisor to join our Guidance and Wellbeing Office (GWO). As an Academic Advisor at SSE, you will work closely with students across our Bachelor and Master programs, providing guidance and support throughout their studies. 
The GWO team consists of two Academic Advisors and one Student Wellbeing Counsellor. Together, the team provides a first point of contact for students who need support related to their studies, their individual educational needs, or challenges that may affect their ability to study. The team also coordinates support for students with specific educational needs. 
As an Academic Advisor, you will: 
Provide individual guidance to students on study-related matters, helping them navigate challenges and make informed decisions about their studies. 
Meet students with a wide range of needs and circumstances and help identify appropriate forms of support. 
Coordinate support for students with specific educational needs and work with relevant colleagues to ensure appropriate arrangements. 
Work closely with the Student Wellbeing Counsellor and the other Academic Advisor to provide coordinated support to students. 
Guide students to other relevant functions or professional support when their needs fall outside the scope of academic advising. 
Collaborate with faculty and other colleagues across SSE on student-related matters. 
Contribute to developing routines, information and ways of working within GWO 
Participate in preventive and student-focused initiatives aimed at creating good conditions for students to succeed in their studies. 

What we offer you
At SSE, you’ll join a small, close-knit GWO team and work across a lively academic community. The role combines one-to-one work with students and collaboration with faculty and colleagues throughout the School. You’ll have the opportunity to shape how GWO supports students, develop its ways of working and contribute to initiatives that strengthen the study experience. It’s a varied role with room to take initiative, build strong working relationships and be part of students’ academic journeys.
About you
You are an attentive, confident communicator who can build trust while maintaining clear professional boundaries. You are comfortable meeting students with varied needs, including in challenging or sensitive situations.
You listen with care, ask thoughtful questions and can work out what kind of guidance or support may be most useful. You are calm and practical when situations are complex, and you enjoy working closely with colleagues who bring different areas of expertise. You are also ready to contribute to initiatives that strengthen students’ wellbeing and study experience.
Qualifications
We are looking for someone with:

A Bachelor’s degree in Study and Career Guidance (Swedish: Studie- och yrkesvägledarexamen).

Experience in student support, academic advising, counselling, education or another role involving professional guidance and individual support.

Spoken and written Swedish and English.

Meritorious

Knowledge of educational support for students with disabilities or other specific educational needs.

Experience using Nais and Ladok.

Experience working in higher education.

Other:
This is a full-time, permanent position with an initial six-month probationary period. The position is based in Stockholm and start date is according to agreement.
We encourage you to apply promptly as we are actively reviewing applications on an ongoing basis. 
We look forward to receiving your application.
About the Stockholm School of Economics
The Stockholm School of Economics is ranked as the top business school in the Nordic and Baltic countries and enjoys a strong international reputation. World-class research forms the foundation of our educational offering, which includes Bachelor, Master, PhD, MBA, and Executive Education programs. Through creativity and collaboration, the Stockholm School of Economics provides an environment where ambitious students and accomplished researchers meet to address contemporary challenges within business and economics, particularly those concerning sustainability, diversity and innovation.
Apart from delivering world class education within business and economics, SSE students are trained to be successful decision makers and leaders of the future. Our educational mission has over the years strengthened SSE students, and you can read more about it here.
SSE is a member of the Stockholm Dual Career Network (SDCN), a collaboration between universities, research institutes and companies in the Stockholm region. Through SDCN, partners of international recruits are offered professional support in establishing their careers in Sweden, including career coaching, networking opportunities, seminars and access to a broad professional network. We recognize the importance of supporting accompanying partners in international relocations and are committed to facilitating a smooth transition for the whole family.
SSE is committed to a balanced gender distribution and values a variety of backgrounds and experiences among our employees. We therefore welcome all applicants regardless of their gender, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, disability, sexual orientation, age, or religion or other beliefs. We strive to have a fair and inclusive recruitment process.

Be a part of the next big thing
Do you thrive on tackling complex challenges? Are you passionate about creating impactful solutions that drive commerce forward? Are you someone who believes in encouraging and elevating those around you?
About Kustom
Kustom was born in 2024 in Stockholm, Sweden, when Klarna Checkout became so successful it earned a life of its own. Since then, we’ve grown into one of Europe’s leading checkout solutions, with a team of more than 100 people all driven by the same mission: giving every business the checkout it deserves.
We believe the best solutions aren't built in isolation. Kustom gives merchants the freedom to shape their own checkout by connecting to a growing network of 100+ partners. We handle the complexity behind the scenes, making sure every shopper enjoys the best possible experience. That way, growth happens freely, without compromises or closed loops.
Today, Kustom serves more than 24,000 merchants across 170 markets and has converted more than 25 million shoppers.
The role
As Legal Counsel, you'll be responsible for Kustom's day-to-day commercial legal work, from merchant and partner agreements and complex negotiations to automating our legal processes. As a trusted internal advisor, you'll lead your matters independently, from first draft to signature.
Commercial work is the core of the role, but it doesn't stop there. You'll also take part in larger projects including M&A and post-acquisition integration and product legal projects covering, among other things, data privacy, payments and consumer legislation.
You'll work in a fast-paced environment where Legal is a key enabler of growth. We use AI as a tool to work efficiently, so we can spend our time where legal judgment matters most. We focus on the risks that are material to the business, and build processes that let standard agreements be signed without legal involvement.
You'll be part of a small legal team in Stockholm and report to the Head of Legal.
Things you’ll be doing
Commercial contracting. Draft, review and negotiate merchant, partner and vendor agreements, from standard terms to bespoke deals with larger counterparties. Your counterparties range from merchants to platform and e-commerce partners, payment service providers, banks and technology vendors.
Advise the business. Be the first point of contact for the commercial organisation and a pragmatic sparring partner to the product, operations, risk and finance teams. Give clear advice fast and if needed negotiate directly with counterparties and their lawyers.
Scale legal with AI. Develop how we use AI in our legal work, and improve templates, playbooks and approval flows so straightforward agreements move without legal involvement.
M&A and integration. Work on M&A together with the Head of Legal, including the legal side of post-acquisition integration, covering everything from contract migration to merchant and partner transitions.
Product legal projects. Work with the product team on larger legal projects, such as data privacy, payments legislation and consumer law.
Corporate and company law. Support on company law matters across the group, including board and shareholder matters and corporate housekeeping.

Skills and experience you’ll need
A Swedish law degree (jur.kand. or juristexamen).
Around three years of experience, either from a top-tier business law firm with a focus on commercial contracts and/or M&A and corporate law or in-house experience from fintech, payments or e-commerce.
A track record of owning negotiations end to end and drafting high-quality agreements.
Hands-on experience of using AI tools in your legal work.
Fluent in Swedish and English, spoken and written.
Experience of data privacy, payments regulation or consumer credit legislation is a plus.

We believe you’ll thrive in this role if you
Take ownership and move things forward without waiting to be told what to do.
Enjoy a high pace and stay structured when many matters compete for your time.
Are commercially minded and know how to balance legal risk against business priorities.
Like working close to the business and can make complex questions simple.
Are always looking for smarter ways of working and see AI as a natural part of how legal work gets done.

Benefits
Secure your future with a competitive pension package, including both national and occupational pension contributions.
Comprehensive health coverage with extensive health insurance, long-term illness protection, and flexible salary exchange options.
Invest in your wellbeing with an annual wellness allowance of 3,000 SEK to spend on the activities that keep you healthy and energized.
More time to enjoy life with an extra day off when major holidays, such as Christmas Eve or New Year’s Eve, fall on a weekend.

A place to grow
At Kustom, you won’t just be another face in the crowd. This is a place where we elevate each other and celebrate success as a team. We believe in our ability to create excellence - and have fun doing it!
We know we set high expectations, but we also know that the road to success isn’t a straight line. We support and encourage each other to try, to fail, to try again. Because that’s how we grow, individually and together.
Does this sound like the place for you?
